walkthrough: Goal: zoom in close to ink fine details and see the lines as crisp as the file they will export to, not enlarged canvas pixels.

Entry: a screen-size canvas at fit with a few Ink Pen lines (the default brush, black). Spread two fingers: the canvas zooms in about them as before (S14); while the fingers move the picture is the one shown so far, enlarged.

What appears: when the fingers stand still or lift, the lines sharpen within a moment: the canvas is drawn again at 2, 4 or 8 times its resolution (whichever is nearest the zoom), the middle of the screen first, the edges a few frames later; an ink edge is about one screen pixel wide at any zoom from about 140 % of the canvas's pixels on. Below that the screen shows the canvas as before.
Turning the canvas with two fingers keeps the lines sharp; panning shows the new edge enlarged for a few frames, then sharp too.
Drawing while zoomed in: the Ink Pen's line is sharp under the tip as it is drawn and stays so when the pen lifts; undo takes it back at once, sharp.
Done: a quick inward pinch fits the canvas again, which shows exactly as before S32.
Nothing to cancel or undo: the view is no step of the drawing; the drawing, its history and exports are unchanged by zooming.
